North Providence Planning Board continues 48-unit Beard Avenue project to Nov. 10
The board also heard a proposal to seek up to $1 million in state community development block grant funding for a facade improvement program and land acquisition near Fruit Hill.
The North Providence Planning Board voted Wednesday, Oct. 14, to continue the proposed 48-unit Beard Avenue development to a new meeting date of Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 6 p.m.
The meeting was held at North Providence Council Chambers, 2000 Smith Street. Attorney Jack McGreen, representing applicant Patriot Builders, asked for the continuance to allow more time for an environmental engineer to respond to issues raised at the previous meeting. "Apparently he was sick for like the last six weeks and we just recently engaged him on Friday," McGreen said.
The applicant agreed to waive the 90-day decision deadline.
TREE ORDINANCE REVIEW Tree Warden Tim Thorp presented a draft update to the town's 1995 tree ordinance, which he said included "significant" changes, as the town seeks continued Tree City USA designation. Board members asked Thorp to provide a document clearly identifying what had been added, modified or removed before they make a recommendation to the town council.
Board member Steve Patassi raised concerns about fallen trees and illegal dumping on town land near North Elmore. "People start littering in the area," he said, asking what plan existed to address it. Thorp said removing deadwood from forested town land would not qualify for grant funding because it serves no ecological benefit, adding that his priority has been "building the canopy in the areas that have no trees."
GRANT FUNDING HEARING Maria Rosa Zacuma, described as CDBG project manager for North Providence, held a public hearing on two potential Community Development Block Grant proposals: a facade improvement program for low-to-moderate income business corridors, and acquisition of land near Fruit Hill for 50-plus housing units and a preserved greenspace. She said the facade program would likely request around $500,000, with individual businesses receiving as much as $50,000.
The board took no action on the funding proposals, as the item was a public hearing only.
The board also voted to continue approval of its Sept. 23 minutes because the stenographer had not yet submitted them, and voted to adjourn.

Board member Steve Patassi raised concerns about fallen trees and illegal dumping on town land near North Elmore.
